authority: AgriN Regenerative Knowledge Registry / CRIDA / ICAR-CAZRI / FAO Conservation Agriculture
evidence_framework: Empirical field validation standards from Indian National Agricultural Research System (NARS)

practices.name: Legume Cover Cropping & Green Manuring
target_conditions: Low soil organic carbon (< 0.50%)
Depleted available nitrogen (< 280 kg/ha)
Post-monsoon or fallow inter-season window
High soil erosion risk
practices.soil_relevance: Builds soil biological nitrogen through symbiotic Rhizobium fixation (50-100 kg N/ha equivalent); adds 15-25 t/ha fresh biomass.
practices.water_relevance: Reduces evaporation losses by 30-40% via live vegetative ground cover; improves rainfall infiltration.
practices.climate_relevance: Buffers rootzone against high surface soil temperatures and heat waves.
constraints: Requires sufficient moisture for initial seed germination
Seed availability of local cultivars like Sesbania or Crotalaria

multi_temporal_pathway.immediate_action: Sow fast-growing green manure (Dhaincha / Sunnhemp / Cowpea) across fallow beds or between wide rows.
multi_temporal_pathway.seasonal_practice: Incorporate biomass into the top 10-15 cm soil at 50% flowering (45-50 days after sowing) prior to main crop transplanting.
multi_temporal_pathway.long_term_goal: Elevate soil organic carbon by 0.15-0.25% over 3-5 rotational seasons, establishing biological nutrient cycling.

practices.expected_objective: Rebuild soil organic matter, fix atmospheric nitrogen naturally, and protect topsoil from erosion.

practices.name: Biochar Soil Conditioning
target_conditions: Coarse sandy soil or low cation exchange capacity (CEC)
Critically low organic carbon (< 0.40%)
Acidic soil (pH < 5.5) or severely leached laterites
Availability of surplus crop residue/biomass
practices.soil_relevance: Stable aromatic recalcitrant carbon with 100+ year half-life; dramatically increases CEC and nutrient holding capacity.
practices.water_relevance: Enhances plant available water capacity (AWC) by 15-25% in porous sandy or weathered soils.
practices.climate_relevance: Prevents open-field residue burning and atmospheric carbon emissions.
constraints: Must be properly charged/inoculated with compost or biofertilizer before application to prevent initial nitrogen immobilization

multi_temporal_pathway.immediate_action: Inoculate biochar with fresh cow dung slurry, vermicompost, and PSB for 14 days before field application.
multi_temporal_pathway.seasonal_practice: Apply charged biochar @ 2-5 tonnes/ha along crop root furrow during primary tillage.
multi_temporal_pathway.long_term_goal: Permanent stabilization of soil organic carbon framework, reducing fertilizer leaching and drought shock vulnerability.

practices.expected_objective: Provide long-term recalcitrant soil carbon matrix, boost microbial colonization, and prevent nutrient leaching.

practices.name: Conservation Tillage & Residue Retention
target_conditions: Heavy black Vertisols prone to crusting/erosion
Cereal-pulse intensive cropping systems
High wind or water erosion zones
Elevated fuel/machinery input costs
practices.soil_relevance: Preserves fungal mycorrhizal hyphal networks and soil macro-aggregates; prevents pulverization of soil structure.
practices.water_relevance: Standing crop stubble captures precipitation, minimizes surface runoff, and conserves residual subsoil moisture.
practices.climate_relevance: Reduces on-farm diesel emissions and mitigates rapid soil moisture evaporation under thermal spikes.
constraints: Requires specialized zero-till / Happy Seeder equipment for seeding through heavy stubble

multi_temporal_pathway.immediate_action: Retain at least 30-40% of previous crop residue standing on the field surface instead of burning or deep moldboard plowing.
multi_temporal_pathway.seasonal_practice: Use zero-till seed-cum-fertilizer drills to deposit seed and basal fertilizer directly into untilled stubble.
multi_temporal_pathway.long_term_goal: Establish continuous undisturbed earthworm and mycorrhizal networks, decreasing soil compaction and runoff by over 50%.

practices.expected_objective: Preserve soil structure, reduce diesel emissions, and maximize seedbed moisture conservation.

practices.name: Crop Diversification & Pulse Rotation
target_conditions: Continuous cereal-cereal or monoculture cash crop cycles
Escalating pest/disease pressure (e.g. pink bollworm, wilt complexes)
Declining fertilizer response ratio
practices.soil_relevance: Breaks host-specific pest/nematode cycles; deep-taproot legumes scavenge subsoil nutrients and solubilize phosphorus.
practices.water_relevance: Alternates deep and shallow rootzones, maximizing water-use efficiency across the profile.
practices.climate_relevance: Spreads market and climate risks; short-duration pulses offer drought-escape mechanisms.
constraints: Farm-gate market procurement certainty for alternative pulse or oilseed crops

multi_temporal_pathway.immediate_action: Introduce a 60-day catch crop (Mungbean / Urad / Mothbean) immediately after rabi harvest.
multi_temporal_pathway.seasonal_practice: Rotate one full parcel per year from cereal monoculture to a legume or oilseed (Pigeonpea, Chickpea, Mustard).
multi_temporal_pathway.long_term_goal: Restore natural ecological pest-predator balance and reduce external synthetic nitrogen dependency by 25-35%.

practices.expected_objective: Disrupt pest and disease life cycles, diversify farm income streams, and replenish soil nitrogen.

practices.name: Organic Mulching & In-Situ Biomass Recycling
target_conditions: Semi-arid or drought-prone rainfall zones
Wide-row spaced crops (Cotton, Sugarcane, Fruit Orchards)
High summer soil temperatures (> 40°C)
practices.soil_relevance: Decomposing mulch gradually feeds topsoil epigeic earthworms and enriches humus layer.
practices.water_relevance: Reduces evaporative moisture loss from soil surface by 40-60%; suppresses weed germination.
practices.climate_relevance: Moderates rootzone thermal fluctuations by 3-5°C during extreme daytime solar radiation.
constraints: Availability of dry straw or bagasse; termite management in dry sandy tracts

multi_temporal_pathway.immediate_action: Spread 5-8 cm layer of dry crop residue, wheat straw, or shredded biomass along crop root zones.
multi_temporal_pathway.seasonal_practice: Replenish mulch layer post-monsoon to conserve receding residual moisture for rabi/summer cycles.
multi_temporal_pathway.long_term_goal: Substantially reduce irrigation frequencies, build spongy surface aggregate layer, and eliminate weed competition.

practices.expected_objective: Conserve soil moisture, suppress weed competition, and buffer root systems against extreme soil temperatures.

practices.name: Vermicomposting & On-Farm Microbial Bio-Formulations
target_conditions: Depleted soil biology or low beneficial microbial biomass
High dependence on synthetic chemical fertilizers
On-farm availability of livestock manure or organic wastes
practices.soil_relevance: Supplies enzymatically active vermicast containing plant growth promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR), auxins, and humic substances.
practices.water_relevance: High humic matter increases water absorption capacity up to 3 times its dry weight.
practices.climate_relevance: Recycles on-farm cattle wastes into stable bio-amendments without methane-generating open lagoons.
constraints: Requires farm labour for maintaining vermicompost bed moisture (60-70%) and shade

multi_temporal_pathway.immediate_action: Set up low-cost shaded vermicompost beds using local earthworm species (Eisenia fetida) and farm crop residue.
multi_temporal_pathway.seasonal_practice: Apply 2.5 tonnes/ha vermicompost as basal manure combined with Trichoderma / Pseudomonas bio-inoculants.
multi_temporal_pathway.long_term_goal: Establish self-sustaining on-farm biological fertility, reducing purchased urea and DAP fertilizer expenses by 30%.

practices.expected_objective: Inoculate soil with beneficial microbial flora, improve nutrient absorption efficiency, and restore earthworm populations.

practices.name: Agroforestry & Field Boundary Tree Windbreaks
target_conditions: Open wind-swept agricultural plains
Severe soil erosion or dry desiccating winds
Marginal farm boundaries or non-arable field borders
practices.soil_relevance: Deep tree roots pump subsoil minerals back to surface via leaf litter; nitrogen-fixing trees enrich perimeter soils.
practices.water_relevance: Windbreaks reduce wind velocity across the crop canopy, cutting crop evapotranspiration rates by 15-20%.
practices.climate_relevance: Provides substantial long-term woody biomass carbon sequestration and microclimate shade.
constraints: Competition with border crop rows if tree branches are not periodically pruned; multi-year maturation timeline

multi_temporal_pathway.immediate_action: Plant multi-purpose native trees (Neem, Gliricidia, Subabul, Teak) along outer field boundaries at 3-5 meter spacing.
multi_temporal_pathway.seasonal_practice: Prune tree branches annually before sowing season and apply loppings as nitrogen-rich green mulch.
multi_temporal_pathway.long_term_goal: Establish a permanent ecological microclimate barrier, generating secondary timber/fodder revenue while protecting field crops.

practices.expected_objective: Reduce wind-driven evapotranspiration, intercept topsoil erosion, and enhance farm-scale biodiversity.

practices.name: Broad Bed and Furrow (BBF) In-Situ Moisture Conservation
target_conditions: Heavy clay soils (Vertisols) with drainage and waterlogging vulnerabilities
Erratic high-intensity monsoon rainfall events
Rainfed kharif crop production (Soybean, Cotton, Groundnut)
practices.soil_relevance: Prevents soil crusting and root asphyxiation during waterlogging; aerates the crop rootzone.
practices.water_relevance: Furrows safely drain excess runoff during heavy downpours and store moisture in subsoil for subsequent dry spells.
practices.climate_relevance: Mitigates crop loss from extreme torrential rainfall followed by dry spells.
constraints: Requires tractor-drawn BBF former / ridge planter attachment at land preparation

multi_temporal_pathway.immediate_action: Lay out broad beds (100 cm width) separated by furrows (30 cm width, 15 cm depth) along 0.2-0.5% grade.
multi_temporal_pathway.seasonal_practice: Plant 2-4 crop rows on the elevated bed, keeping furrows open for drainage and supplemental irrigation.
multi_temporal_pathway.long_term_goal: Eliminate moisture-stress crop failures, prevent topsoil erosion, and ensure optimal aeration in heavy clay soils.

practices.expected_objective: Prevent waterlogging during heavy rainfall while simultaneously recharging groundwater for dry spell resilience.
